DSA_QUESTIONS.title: Maximum Subarray · LeetCode #53
DSA_QUESTIONS.hint: At each value, compare starting a new subarray with extending the previous one.
DSA_QUESTIONS.description: Read a line of integers. Print the largest sum of any contiguous non-empty subarray.
DSA_QUESTIONS.reference_solution:
a=list(map(int,input().split()))
current=best=a[0]
for value in a[1:]:
    current=max(value,current+value)
    best=max(best,current)
print(best)

DSA_QUESTIONS.title: Product of Array Except Self · LeetCode #238
DSA_QUESTIONS.hint: Build prefix products in one pass and combine with suffix products in another.
DSA_QUESTIONS.description: Read integers on one line. Print the product of all values except the value at each index. Do not use division.
DSA_QUESTIONS.reference_solution:
a=list(map(int,input().split())); out=[1]*len(a)
prefix=1
for i,x in enumerate(a): out[i]=prefix; prefix*=x
suffix=1
for i in range(len(a)-1,-1,-1): out[i]*=suffix; suffix*=a[i]
print(*out)

DSA_QUESTIONS.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters · LeetCode #3
DSA_QUESTIONS.hint: Maintain a sliding window and the most recent index for each character.
DSA_QUESTIONS.description: Read a string. Print the length of its longest substring with no repeated characters.
DSA_QUESTIONS.reference_solution:
s=input().rstrip('\n'); last={}; start=0; best=0
for i,ch in enumerate(s):
    if ch in last and last[ch]>=start: start=last[ch]+1
    last[ch]=i; best=max(best,i-start+1)
print(best)

DSA_QUESTIONS.title: Top K Frequent Elements · LeetCode #347
DSA_QUESTIONS.hint: Count frequencies first, then order by frequency; define how ties are handled.
DSA_QUESTIONS.description: Read integers on one line and k on the next. Print the k most frequent values, highest frequency first; break ties by ascending value.
DSA_QUESTIONS.reference_solution:
from collections import Counter
a=list(map(int,input().split())); k=int(input())
print(*[v for v,_ in sorted(Counter(a).items(),key=lambda x:(-x[1],x[0]))[:k]])

DSA_QUESTIONS.title: Binary Search · LeetCode #704
DSA_QUESTIONS.description: Read a sorted list of integers on line one and a target on line two. Print its index, or -1.
DSA_QUESTIONS.hint: Keep a search interval and discard half on each comparison.
DSA_QUESTIONS.reference_solution:
a=list(map(int,input().split())); t=int(input()); lo=0; hi=len(a)-1
while lo<=hi:
 m=(lo+hi)//2
 if a[m]==t: print(m); break
 if a[m]<t: lo=m+1
 else: hi=m-1
else: print(-1)

DSA_QUESTIONS.title: Majority Element · LeetCode #169
DSA_QUESTIONS.description: Read integers on one line. Print the element appearing more than n/2 times.
DSA_QUESTIONS.hint: Boyer-Moore voting finds a candidate in constant extra space.
DSA_QUESTIONS.reference_solution:
a=list(map(int,input().split())); c=None; n=0
for x in a:
 if n==0: c=x
 n+=1 if x==c else -1
print(c)

machine_learning.title: Binary Classification Metrics
machine_learning.description: Read true labels on line one and predicted labels on line two. Print precision and recall to 3 decimals. Treat label 1 as positive; if a denominator is zero, print 0.000.
machine_learning.reference_solution:
y=list(map(int,input().split())); p=list(map(int,input().split()))
tp=sum(a==1 and b==1 for a,b in zip(y,p))
fp=sum(a==0 and b==1 for a,b in zip(y,p))
fn=sum(a==1 and b==0 for a,b in zip(y,p))
precision=tp/(tp+fp) if tp+fp else 0
recall=tp/(tp+fn) if tp+fn else 0
print(f'{precision:.3f} {recall:.3f}')

machine_learning.title: Feature Standardization
machine_learning.description: Read numeric features on one line. Print z-scores using population standard deviation, each rounded to 3 decimals. If all values are equal, print zeros.
machine_learning.reference_solution:
import math
x=list(map(float,input().split())); mean=sum(x)/len(x)
std=math.sqrt(sum((v-mean)**2 for v in x)/len(x))
print(*(f'{(v-mean)/std:.3f}' if std else '0.000' for v in x))
